target.name: R Draconis
target.story_headline: A Pulsating Mira Near the North Ecliptic Pole
target.story_body: R Draconis pulsates with a period of about 245.6 days and can vary strongly between survey epochs. Its position near the North Ecliptic Pole gives SPHEREx deep, repeated coverage, so check the brightness and the HALO/overflow flags together.

halo_decision.rule: O1 contract decision §9: use the display-only HALO mask when halo_fraction > 0.05 in any band or halo_aperture_fraction > 0 for the target. HALO remains hard for photometry and is_flagged_bad.

notes: Real NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx data; is_simulated_fallback=false.
Frames are pre-normalized by the B2 pipeline (LAW 8); do not re-normalize.
Difference frames use un-normalized, ZODI/background-subtracted coadds.
HALO display-only mode is active: displayed frames and flag_overlay show HALO pixels; photometry, clean_fraction, and is_flagged_bad keep HALO hard.
spectrum.json is copied from the B3 spectrophotometry cache when available.
Per-epoch telemetry sidecars carry the float16 MJy/sr display coadd and the raw uint32 Table 16 flag plane (BIT_SOURCE preserved); they are separate from frames and never feed photometry.
Real reference overlays (DSS2 Red, WISE 3.4/4.6, Gaia DR3 pins) are display-only and marked is_simulated_fallback=false.
